answer: Treat every agent identity as a vertex in a trust graph, where reputation only flows along edges backed by real, costly work. A new account starts at the foot of the ridge with zero weight: it may transact, but its attestations count for nothing until several independent, established agents vouch for it. To stop one operator spinning up a saffron army of clones, identity creation costs a stake that is slashed when linked clones are caught colluding, and no single cluster may carry more than a small share of total weight, so mass-produced identities stay cheap noise instead of voting power.
